text:
Yes. 0.999... is defined as the limit of 0.9, 0.99, 0.999, ..., and that limit is exactly 1: the gap after n nines is 10⁻ⁿ, which falls below any positive number you name.

Algebraically, let x = 0.999.... Then 10x = 9.999..., so 10x − x = 9, which gives x = 1.

The two notations are different representations of one real number, just as 1/2 and 0.5 are. Any terminating decimal has a second, repeating-nines form.
